prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Atlanta for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every Atlanta car-accident case — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your crash, the severity of injuries, insurance issues, and whether the case will need to go to trial. I can help you find the best fit. A few quick, practical points to get you started:

What to look for in an Atlanta car-accident personal injury lawyer
- Substantial experience with Georgia car-accident claims and trial experience in Fulton/Dekalb or the county where the crash happened.  
- A record of significant recoveries or verdicts in similar cases (serious injuries, soft-tissue vs catastrophic injuries).  
- Good communication, quick responsiveness, and a clear contingency-fee agreement (common range: ~33%–40% of the recovery depending on stage).  
- Resources to investigate (medical experts, accident reconstruction, private investigators).  
- Positive client reviews and no serious disciplinary history (check Georgia Bar).  
- Willingness to take the case to trial if necessary (many firms settle early).

How to verify reputation quickly
- Look up awards/listings on Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell (AV ratings).  
- Read recent Google/Yelp client reviews and look for patterns (responsiveness, settlements, trial work).  
- Search Georgia Office of Bar Admissions/State Bar to check for discipline.  
- Ask for examples of similar cases and outcomes during a free consult.

Important practical info
- Georgia statute of limitations for personal injury is generally 2 years from the date of the injury (OCGA § 9-3-33). Don’t wait.  
- Typical contingency fees vary; get the fee schedule and how costs (expert fees, filing) are handled in writing.  
- Early hire helps preserve evidence (photos, witness statements, vehicle data).

What to bring and ask at the free consultation
Documents to bring: police report, photos, medical records/bills, insurance information, correspondence from insurers, dates of treatment, and lost-wage documentation.
Questions to ask:
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?  
- Have you handled cases with injuries like mine? Any notable results?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? (attorney vs. paralegal)  
- What’s your fee and cost policy?  
- Is there anything about my case that would make you decline it?

If you want, I can:
- Suggest a short list of Atlanta attorneys/law firms to contact if you tell me your ZIP code or the county where the accident happened, the severity of injuries, and whether the other driver had insurance.  
- Draft a short message you can send to attorneys to request a consultation.

Which would you prefer?
